$comment: Read-only inspection commands, merged by hand into ~/.claude/settings.json (allow and ask; the installer does not apply this file; README 'Permissions baseline'). Claude Code matches a rule against the command text as written (whitespace collapsed, quotes and backslashes kept), and an allow rule ending in * covers every flag of its command, also when the command runs through xargs. The ask rules below (ask wins over allow) therefore catch only the plain spelling of a flag: a quoted or escaped flag (--kube"config"), a combined short flag (-As) or flags passed through xargs get past them. They are a backstop, not a boundary. The rule for this file: an allow wildcard belongs here only if its residual risk is listed below and in the README; a rule whose flags can run a program from the clone belongs in permissions-trusted-repo.json (so helm template, whose --post-renderer runs one, is there). git diff/log/show/blame have no rule: Claude Code's built-in read-only check allows their safe forms and asks for the rest (--output=FILE). git fetch and terraform fmt -check are allowed in exact forms only (git fetch --upload-pack runs a command, and a later -check=false makes fmt rewrite files). Ask rules: kubectl/helm --kubeconfig (a kubeconfig's exec credential plugin runs a program), kubectl --server/-s and helm --kube-apiserver (send the kubeconfig's credentials, such as an exec plugin's token, to another API server), helm --kube-token, kubectl --cache-dir and --profile (writes ./profile.pprof; the rule also matches --profile-output), helm --post-renderer/--output-dir/--repository-cache/--repository-config/--registry-config/--dependency-update, terraform plan -out/-generate-config-out. Residual risks, accepted on purpose: a disguised --kubeconfig runs a kubeconfig's exec plugin, a disguised --server or --kube-apiserver sends the cluster token elsewhere, and a disguised write flag writes a file; terraform plan runs the configuration's providers and external data sources (code from the clone) against the configured backend (it does not apply), and terraform validate/show/state show start the provider plugins in .terraform/; kubectl get, helm get and terraform show/output can print secrets into the session; jq reads any file (it stays because az ... | jq pipes need every segment allowed); git fetch talks to the network (it writes only .git/); shell redirection is checked apart from the rules: Claude Code 2.1.284 asks before > file writes a file (acceptEdits allows it inside the working directory, like any edit), and a version without that check would let > file write after any rule. Left out: terraform providers lock/mirror (write files). Build and test runners live in permissions-trusted-repo.json.
